liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): The explosion into this song is described as one for the books; This song twists and runs so hard it feels like it will cut you [13][14]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): A half-hour take of this song and a monster Dark Star version are highlighted [12]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): A hot CE>TOO>CE sequence is present and can't be missed [17]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Check out the 'Playin'' tease near the end, perhaps the earliest extant riff of a later classic [18]
- **Cryptical Reprise** (1 review): Dropped from so high and quiet that the detonation will slay [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-04-15.aud.sbd-patch.komar.miller.31939.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 123 min; rated 2.29/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.miller.31435.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 16 songs; 122 min; rated 4.5/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Jerry's vocals are great, Pig is on, and the man's axe sounds great; Recording is excellent given circumstances, with Jerry's guitar out front; Audience recording is surprisingly listenable for the era, though quality is not quibbled over [11][12][13][17][20]
- **gd1969-04-15.aud.komar.miller.31523.flac16**: audience recording; 16 songs; 122 min; rated 3.89/5 by 9 [3]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.komar.31672.sbefail.flac16**: audience recording; 15 songs; 122 min [4]
- **gd69-04-15.sbd.cotsman.6288.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 30 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [8]. Said about its sound: Short segment has okay sound, serving as filler for another show from the same venue [9]

## Around the show

- A woman talks throughout the song, reflecting the audience perspective with a handheld microphone [10]
- This is a better show than Dick's 16, and Stephen into Eleven is preferred [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-04-15.aud.sbd-patch.komar.miller.31939.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Aiwa hand-held microphone -> Master Reel (Aiwa 5" reel-to-reel) -> Alesis Masterlink 9600 -> Hard Drive -> CD [1]. Also: Morning Dew through Doin' That Rag patched from SBD to cassette to DAT to CD; Digital transfer by Jeremy Garrett at Rainbow Music, Omaha, in September 2005 [1]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.miller.31435.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Jeremy Garrett, Scott Allan and Charlie Miller; source: Audience: Aiwa hand-held Microphone [2]. Also: Taped on Formula 10 audiotape, 1/2 mil Mylar, 3 3/4 ips, 2-track mono [2]
- **gd1969-04-15.aud.komar.miller.31523.flac16**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Aiwa hand-held microphone -> Master Reel (Aiwa 5" reel-to-reel) -> Alesis Masterlink 9600 -> Hard Drive -> CD [3]. Also: Digital transfer by Jeremy Garrett at Rainbow Music, Omaha, in September 2005 [3]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.komar.31672.sbefail.flac16**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Bob Bihlmayer; source: portable Aiwa 5" reel-to-reel, stock Aiwa hand-held microphone; "Automatic Volume Control" (compressor/limiter?) switch ON. [4]. Also: Real-time transfer with no edits, EQ flat, and no boosts or filters applied [4]
- **gd69-04-15.sbd.cotsman.6288.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [8]
